reason: The cited evidence does not involve NbMoTaW or any refractory BCC HEA; it discusses ductility in a dual-phase AlCoCrFeNi (E2), SRO in CrCoNi (E1), and thermomechanical processing of a lightweight Ti-based MEA (E3–E5). No evidence supports the key premises about bimodal grain structures improving ductility or irradiation resistance in NbMoTaW, nor the specific processing parameters for this alloy.
premises: Hot rolling near 1600 °C followed by cold rolling and rapid annealing can produce a bimodal grain structure in NbMoTaW.
A bimodal grain structure with ultrafine and coarse grains improves room-temperature ductility in BCC HEAs.
Coarse grains maintain high-temperature strength in BCC HEAs.
Grain boundaries enhance defect recombination and irradiation resistance in BCC HEAs.
Thermomechanical processing parameters (e.g., 50% cold rolling, 850–900 °C rapid annealing) are transferable to NbMoTaW.
